messages.author: alice
messages.content: INCIDENT: elevated 500 rate on /api/search. Started ~09:05 UTC. PagerDuty firing. Ticket: PROD-101

messages.author: bob
messages.content: On it, pulling logs now

messages.author: mia
messages.content: I see it too. Error rate is ~18% of search requests. Most requests fine.

messages.author: alice
messages.content: Sampled the failing requests — they all have `q=` with an empty value in the query string

messages.author: bob
messages.content: Checking Redis cache layer first — maybe cache is returning corrupt data for empty keys

messages.author: mia
messages.content: Redis metrics look normal. Hit rate is fine, no errors in the Redis logs

messages.author: bob
messages.content: ok Redis is clean, not the cache. Let me look at the actual stack trace

messages.author: bob
messages.content:
Got it. Stack trace from sentry:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/search.py", line 14, in search_users
    prefix = term[0].lower()
IndexError: string index out of range
```

messages.author: alice
messages.content: so it's a Python IndexError on `term[0]` in search.py — crashes when the search term is an empty string

messages.author: mia
messages.content: right. line 14 does `prefix = term[0].lower()` without first checking if term is empty. if term == "" then term[0] raises IndexError

messages.author: bob
messages.content: should we check DB connection pool? I also saw some connection timeout warnings earlier this week

messages.author: alice
messages.content: those were unrelated — that was the migration job last Wednesday. This is clearly the search.py IndexError

messages.author: mia
messages.content: agreed. DB pool is fine. Let's stay focused on the root cause: empty term hits term[0] and crashes

messages.author: bob
messages.content: Let me try triggering a reindex on the search backend — maybe stale index entries are producing empty terms

messages.author: mia
messages.content: reindex won't help here — the empty term is coming from the HTTP request itself, not from index data. client is sending ?q= with no value

messages.author: bob
messages.content: ran the reindex anyway. errors are still happening. you're right, not a search index issue

messages.author: alice
messages.content: ok so the fix is straightforward: in search_users, add a guard at the top — `if not term: return []` — before we ever try to access term[0]

messages.author: mia
messages.content: yes exactly. the fix is: add `if not term: return []` right at the start of search_users, before the `prefix = term[0].lower()` line. empty query should return empty results, not crash

messages.author: bob
messages.content: +1 on the fix. ship it as a PR to acme/webapp, get it reviewed and merged, then close PROD-101
